paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Israel asked the LORD before they swung a single sword. Joshua was gone, and the job was big, so they asked who should go first. The LORD answered, "Judah shall go up," and then added, "Indeed, I have delivered the land into their hands." (Judges 1:2) When God has already said where to go, that's the best place to start, and it's the same for you, baker.

Now look at how Judah went. They didn't go alone. They told the Simeonites, "Come up with us…" and promised, "And we likewise will go with you to your territory." (Judges 1:3) Later they teamed up again at Zephath (Judges 1:17). Sure, I can bake a batch by myself, but it's a lot more fun when somebody's holding the other end of the tray!

And here's the part that hit me. "The LORD was with Judah, and they took possession of the hill country; but they could not drive out the inhabitants of the plains because they had chariots of iron." (Judges 1:19) Real wins and real limits sit side by side in the same verse. Friend, you can follow God well and still run into a stubborn plain or two, so keep your apron on, because this story isn't over.
